story.title: Built on 27 million files and a drawer of old drives.
story.p1: BackDown began as a one-off job: consolidate years of old disks onto one archive and wipe the rest. The hard part was never copying bytes.
story.p2: Five of six drives held generations of the same data. The most valuable thing on them, a mail server's archive, only turned up by reading the shell script that once backed it up. And 5.9 TB of the biggest drive was quietly duplicating itself.
story.p3: No backup tool would have told us any of that. So we built one that does.
story.s1_label: files indexed, with every job resumable when a USB drive dropped off the bus
story.s2_label: of storage read and hashed, with source drives mounted read-only throughout
story.s3_label: of the biggest drive found duplicating itself
story.s4_label: drives wiped, each only after every byte was hash-verified elsewhere
how.title: Plug in everything. Get answers, not a vault.
how.intro: Backup tools answer "can I restore this file?" BackDown also answers "what do I have, what's duplicated, and what's safe to delete?"
how.s1_title: Point it at every drive you own
how.s1_body: Old laptops, NAS shares, the USB disk in the drawer. Sources are mounted read-only and tracked by serial number, never by /dev/sdX, so the wrong disk is never touched.
how.s2_body: Tiered hashing checks size first, then a quick sample, then a full SHA-256, so it only fully reads files that could be duplicates. If a drive disconnects or the machine reboots, you lose the file in flight, not the night.
how.s3_title: You get a verdict for every drive
how.s3_body: What's on it, what each folder is, what's duplicated across every source, and a verdict: safe to wipe, or copy these 212 GB first. Nothing is deleted without a verified copy.
features.title: The intelligence other backup tools leave out.
features.intro: Borg, restic and Time Machine are excellent vaults. BackDown adds the layer that tells you what you're actually storing.
features.legend: BackDown is pre-release, so each feature is marked with its status.
features.f1_body: Not just inside one repository. Each new drive is checked against everything already indexed. Hardlinks and symlinks are accounted for, so reclaim figures are real.
features.f2_title: Proof a drive is safe to wipe
features.f2_body: Either every file has a SHA-256-identical copy elsewhere, or you get the list of files that don't. Every copy and deletion is journaled against a verified hash.
features.f3_body: Every long job resumes where it stopped. Flaky USB enclosures are remounted automatically, and jobs run one per spindle so a single disk never thrashes.
features.f4_body: Maildirs, Time Machine sets, phone backups, home directories, disk images, git repos, SQL dumps and cloud exports, each with a date range and size. Regenerable caches are flagged and skipped.
features.f5_body: BackDown reads the rsync scripts, sync markers and backup metadata that record your data's history. It can say "rsynced from your mail server on 31 May 2020," not just "some files."
features.f6_title: A web UI you'll actually open
features.f6_body: Live progress, interactive size trees, duplicate tables and per-drive verdicts, served locally by the daemon, in light and dark.
features.f7_body: Mailboxes appear as threaded mail, photos as a gallery, SQL dumps as schemas. Disk images mount read-only. Search every backup and drive at once.
features.f8_body: Content-defined chunking, zstd compression and client-side encryption, verified on a schedule, to local disks, SFTP, S3 or B2.
features.f9_body: Signed, append-only manifests of every copy, move and delete, a record you can hand to an auditor or a court.
privacy.title: Your data stays on your disks.
privacy.intro: Most backup services start by uploading everything. BackDown starts from the opposite end.
privacy.p1_body: The local edition makes no network requests. It needs no account and sends no telemetry.
privacy.p2_body: Drives being analysed are mounted read-only, so a flaky enclosure can't corrupt the data you're trying to save.
privacy.p3_body: Nothing is removed unless a copy with a matching hash is already in the journal.
privacy.p4_body: The optional team dashboard sees metadata only. Your files leave your machines only if you add a cloud backup target.
pricing.title: Free for what you have. Paid for what it knows.
pricing.intro: The core engine will be source-available and free forever. The intelligence, forensic and fleet features are paid, priced per machine rather than per gigabyte.
pricing.fine: Planned launch pricing in US dollars. It may change before release, and early-access members will hear first.
download.title: BackDown for Linux, macOS and Windows.
download.intro: The command-line preview is out now for Linux, macOS and Windows. The desktop app follows with version 1.0.
download.linux_body: Command-line preview: one static binary each for x86-64 and ARM64.
download.macos_body: Command-line preview: one binary for Apple silicon and Intel.
download.note: Every release comes with SHA-256 checksums. Preview builds aren't signed yet: on macOS, run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown once; on Windows, SmartScreen may ask you to confirm.
